applies_why: The judge text resolves the Romans 1:3 paternity collision by treating the absence of an explicit textual resolution as UNDERDETERMINED, which is the kind of explicit-verse test K-C governs.
quote: D6 vs C4 (Romans 1:3): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] section A.1-2 and [CR3] Link 6 premises 1-3, where descent according to the flesh is weighed against conception of the Holy Ghost without explicit textual resolution of paternity.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse: (1) compare the whole chains' footing even without an explicit contrary verse; (2) treat absence of an explicit textual resolution as underdetermined. I adopt (1).
why: The judge labels the matter UNDERDETERMINED for lack of an explicit textual resolution, which is the retired stating-verse test and fails K-C's required chain-against-chain footing.
